messages:
From: Chris Lane <support@nebulaai.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Mar 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Production regressions impacting inference latency & errors (account: NebulaAI)

Hi Stephanie,

We started seeing a sustained latency increase and higher 5xx rates across our LLM endpoints beginning around 03/09 02:30 UTC. This is impacting our UI timeouts and batch jobs — roughly 18% of requests are now experiencing >2s tail latency and error rate opened up to 4.2%.

We raised a support ticket but this is customer-impacting at scale. Can Redwood confirm:
- root cause and timeline to remediation
- whether this qualifies under SLAs for credits/compensation
- short-term mitigation steps we can apply on our side

I’ve attached a short CSV (nebula-incident-log-0309.csv) with representative requests and timestamps. We need an exec-level point of contact — cc’ing Maya (CTO) who is looped in.

Thanks,
Chris Lane
Head of Ops, NebulaAI

Date: Mon, 09 Mar 2026 14:35:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Production regressions — preliminary findings

Quick update from infra: we saw a spike in scheduling latency on our shared routing tier coincident with a kernel selection regression introduced in the 03/08 deploy. Key observations: 
- CPU-side preemption increased during high-concurrency bursts; KV-cache eviction patterns changed for models Nebula uses (gpt-compat-13b).
- Error 502/503 correlate to an overflow of the request queue on two hosts in the pool; we auto-failed them but customer traffic saw the tail.
- Attached: redwood-slo-metrics-0309-0311.pdf (SLO dashboards and per-host traces)

Immediate mitigations applied at 14:10 UTC: rolled back the 03/08 kernel change on routing fleet and increased short-term capacity for Nebula’s dedicated pool. Early signs show tail latency improving but we still need to validate full regression window and token exposure to compute credits.

-Jonas
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime

Maya / Chris — thanks for the call this morning. Summary and next steps below (agreement reached during exec call):

Summary of findings:
- Root cause: 03/08 kernel selection change plus transient queue pressure on shared routing hosts; rollback reduced tail latency within 4 hours but customer traffic saw a 30-hour window of degraded performance (03/08 02:20 UTC — 03/09 08:20 UTC).
- Impact: Nebula experienced elevated tail latency and ~3.8% higher error rate during the window. Naomi attached precise token exposure and a calculation doc during the call (shared link).

Commercial remediation agreed:
- Redwood will issue a one-time credit equivalent to 21% of Nebula’s March invoice reflecting pro-rata impacted usage. Credit will appear on Nebula’s next invoice and be accompanied by a short explanation doc for their finance team.
- Redwood will implement a pinned-model routing policy for Nebula for 90 days at no additional charge and weekly operational reviews for 3 months.
- DocuSign: both parties to sign the make-good term sheet — link: https://app.docusign.com/NEB-MAKEGOOD-2026

Attachments: redwood-makegood-term-sheet-NEB.docx, redwood-slo-metrics-0309-0311.pdf

Please confirm acceptance by signing the DocuSign envelope; we will arrange internal accounting to apply the credit within two billing cycles after signature. If legal needs any language tweaks, loop in legal@redwood.com and we’ll fast-track.

Thanks for working through this — we’ll continue to monitor the routing fleet and send a postmortem within 7 business days.

-Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
